verdict.rationale: Mastra Code documents recurring prompts that can be created, run, paused, resumed or deleted, plus a Goals feature that keeps the agent working across turns until a judge model marks the objective complete. Its headless mode with auto-approved tools also suits unattended CI and server runs. The evidence does not show where or how recurring prompts execute, so true background autonomy (running detached or when the TUI is closed) is not established. missing for 10: documentation of how recurring prompts are scheduled and executed in the background (detached or persistent runner, schedule syntax), confirmation that automations run without an active session, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Create, run, pause, resume, or delete recurring prompts
Keep Mastra Code working across turns until a judge model marks the objective complete or waits for your input.
`runMC` never calls `process.exit` and never writes to global streams, so it is safe to embed in CI scripts and servers.
